bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Machine Learning Engineer Salary Conversion

If you are a machine learning engineer in Australia, you may see job ads quoting an hourly rate or an annual salary. Converting between the two is straightforward, but you need to account for the standard working week, casual loading, tax, and superannuation. This guide explains how to calculate your annual gross pay from an hourly rate, using the Fair Work Commission’s National Minimum Wage as a baseline and the Australian Tax Office’s 2026–27 tax rates.

The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For full-time employees, we assume 38 hours per week, which is the ordinary hours under the National Employment Standards. This assumption applies throughout this article unless stated otherwise.

### How to Convert an Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Start with your hourly rate. Multiply it by 38 (hours per week) and then by 52 (weeks per year). For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. The annual equivalent is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,267.04 (rounded).

If you are a casual employee, you receive a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. The casual minimum wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). Annual casual pay would be:

$33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,333.80.

You can also calculate your fortnightly pay by multiplying the weekly amount by two. For the minimum wage, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs Market Rates

The National Minimum Wage applies to award/agreement-free employees. Most machine learning engineers are covered by an award (such as the Professional Employees Award 2020) or an enterprise agreement, which may set higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award that include minimum hourly rates, allowances, and penalty rates.

However, machine learning engineer salaries are typically well above award rates due to high demand. The Australian Bureau of Statistics’ Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 shows full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, which equates to about $108,352 per year. Many machine learning engineers earn significantly more, often in the range of $120,000 to $180,000 annually, depending on experience and location.

### Tax and Medicare Levy on Your Annual Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: 45% on excess over $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies to your taxable income. For a machine learning engineer earning $150,000 per year, the tax estimate (excluding Medicare) would be:

- First $18,200: $0
- $18,201 to $45,000: $4,020 (15% of $26,800)
- $45,001 to $135,000: $27,000 (30% of $90,000)
- $135,001 to $150,000: $5,550 (37% of $15,000)
- Total tax: $36,570
- Medicare levy (2% of $150,000): $3,000
- Total tax and Medicare: $39,570

Your take-home pay would be approximately $110,430 per year, or $9,202.50 per month. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more detailed breakdown.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is not deducted from your salary; it is paid on top by your employer. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a $150,000 salary, your employer would contribute an additional $18,000 in super. This amount is not included in your annual gross pay for tax purposes but is part of your total remuneration package.

### Putting It All Together: A Machine Learning Engineer Example

Let’s say you are offered a machine learning engineer role at $75 per hour. Assuming 38 hours per week, your annual gross salary is:

$75 × 38 × 52 = $148,200.

Your fortnightly gross pay would be $5,700 ($2,850 per week). After tax (using the 2026–27 rates) and Medicare, your annual take-home pay would be approximately $108,000, depending on your exact circumstances. Your employer would also pay $17,784 in super on top.

Remember that this calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Actual machine learning engineer salaries vary; check job advertisements or the ABS for current market data. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database provides official minimum rates for award-covered roles.

### Use Our Timesheet for Your Own Calculation

To convert your own hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures, try [the timesheet](/). You can enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. The tool will show you gross annual pay, tax estimates, and super contributions. It’s a quick way to see what a machine learning engineer salary looks like in real terms.

For more information on award rates and pay guides, visit the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) page. You can also explore our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) topic for additional examples.
